scope: binary_to_term/1 bounded uncompressed data ETF profile; native-derived parser and real process terms, with transactional atom publication.
adaptations: Snapshot aligned or unaligned byte-length binary input in the owning accounted domain before any collection. Decode one versioned term with trailing bytes permitted, using temporary pointer tags and the shared ETF arena. Unknown tags are badarg; known unadmitted families refuse explicitly.

Stage atom identities without publication, validate and order maps after atom patching, size and copy the completed data graph into moving process storage preserving heap credit. Commit atoms only after successful copying; no fallible work follows publication. Abort atom staging before reclaiming earlier preparation records.

Reserve conservative hash-chain/rehash and ownership-registry work before staging. Track exact live allocation record counts; arena allocation reserves quadratic teardown credit incrementally for non-LIFO offheap/staging interleavings. Runtime flatmap comparisons charge their actual traversal, while HAMT preparation reserves bounded hash/sort/build work before construction. This is a work-unit policy, not a hard CPU-time guarantee or a throughput claim.

Compressed ETF, legacy floats, local and external funs, record/cache/distribution encodings and PID/port/reference identities remain explicitly outside this initial data profile. No autoload, ambient identity creation or unsupported value fabrication is used. Input/preparation/term-size limits and the restricted HAMT key/collision profile still apply.

Tests cover actual compiled calls, unaligned input, trailing consumption, malformed/truncated inputs, duplicate maps, HAMT copy and collection, unchanged source on failure, heap credit, atom rollback under allocation/quota/work denial, real worker thresholds/reuse/peer survival/reclamation, and all tested final balances. Fresh-atom work prefixes are measured at the primitive boundary: successful atom publication remains visible if a later return-path instruction exhausts the invocation budget. No whole-invocation state rollback is promised.
